records.title: Staudinger macromolecular theory through prolonged resistance
records.sourceNativeSummary: Staudinger argued in the early 1920s that polymers were true very-large covalently bonded molecules/long chains despite substantial chemical opposition. Later synthesis/measurement made the macromolecular representation productive and foundational for polymer chemistry.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A correct structural hypothesis can remain low-tractability when available measurement/model assumptions favor alternatives; later success cannot be used as evidence that contemporary opponents had no rational uncertainty.

sources.supports: early-1920s macromolecule claim and long-chain polymer basis
macromolecule controversy and constructive polymer synthesis

records.title: Continental drift through continued rejection despite accumulating observations
records.sourceNativeSummary: Wegener’s 1915 continental-drift synthesis connected coastline fit, fossils, geology and paleoclimate but lacked a convincing physical mechanism and was strongly rejected by much of geology during his lifetime.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Multi-line observational coherence can be insufficient for adoption when the proposed dynamics appear physically implausible. Later plate tectonics does not retroactively supply Wegener with mechanisms unavailable in HD4.

sources.supports: 1915 theory, multi-domain evidence and severe contemporary rejection

records.title: Insulin potency units and transnational biological standardization
records.sourceNativeSummary: Variable biological potency made insulin dosing incomparable across preparations. University, industrial and international actors developed biological units and standards so clinical effects could be reproduced across lots/manufacturers.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A standard coordinates representation and action but does not guarantee purity, access or optimal dose for each patient; standardization solves a defined comparability problem rather than every quality problem.

sources.supports: making the insulin unit and transnational/industrial standardization

records.title: International radio-frequency allocation and aviation/radio safety coordination
records.sourceNativeSummary: Rapid radio growth created interference and cross-border coordination pressure. The 1927 Washington conference introduced the first international table of frequency allocations; by 1944 the Chicago Convention established principles for safe/orderly international civil aviation and future ICAO coordination.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Formal allocation/convention is not effective compliance; radio congestion, sovereignty, technical compatibility and postwar implementation remained separate operational problems.

sources.supports: 1944 Chicago Convention and international aviation coordination

records.title: Tetraethyl-lead worker poisoning and public-health controversy
records.sourceNativeSummary: Tetraethyl lead solved engine knock and enabled higher-compression performance, but concentrated production caused severe worker poisoning/deaths almost immediately. A temporary suspension and later voluntary standard addressed acute workplace exposure while broad environmental harm remained outside the prevailing evaluator.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Local engine performance and even improved refinery workplace practices did not establish population-level safety. The evaluator’s boundary—acute factory poisoning versus chronic diffuse exposure—changed the apparent verdict.

sources.supports: 1921 TEL success, 1924 worker deaths, 1925 suspension and later standards

records.title: Radium-dial occupational poisoning and radiation-protection correction
records.sourceNativeSummary: Workers painting luminous radium dials ingested radium after being instructed to point brushes with their lips. Injuries, litigation and quantitative body/radon measurements helped overturn employer safety claims and strengthened occupational radiation awareness.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A useful luminous material and existing radiation standards did not imply safe work practice. Employer assurances were representations contradicted by biological/electrometric evidence.

sources.supports: dial-worker exposure, measurements and court evidence
factory practice, illness and measurement correction

records.title: Corn-steep liquor, strain search and deep-tank fermentation as hidden penicillin scale complements
records.sourceNativeSummary: Once penicillin’s clinical value was clearer, U.S. production still depended on fermentation engineering, aeration/agitation, productive media such as corn steep liquor, strain search and downstream recovery. These less-famous changes turned scarce laboratory drug into mass supply.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The complement did not discover penicillin’s antibacterial effect and should not own the whole trajectory; conversely, discovery/clinical proof without these process capabilities could not produce the wartime consequence.

sources.supports: corn steep liquor, strain search and deep-tank fermentation
government-industry process scale-up and wartime production
